questions.question: What is conflict in a narrative?
choices: a struggle that creates tension around a goal or value

questions.question: A student argues with a friend about keeping a promise. What kind of conflict is central?
A hiker must cross a flooded trail before nightfall. What conflict is emphasized?
A student wants to confess a mistake but fears embarrassment. Which conflict is this?
A community challenges a rule that excludes some residents. What conflict is shown?
A repair worker tries to stop an automated system from shutting down a hospital. Which conflict fits?
Two siblings compete to lead a project and disagree about its direction. What conflict is this?
A character debates whether to reveal a friend’s secret to prevent harm. What makes the struggle internal?
choices: competing values and choices within one character

questions.question: A character wants to preserve a family tradition while the town pressures everyone to abandon it. Which conflict is strongest?
A wildfire threatens a town, and neighbors disagree about evacuation. What is the main external force?
A story includes an argument between teammates and the captain’s private guilt. What does this show?
choices: every story has only one conflict
a narrative can develop more than one conflict
internal conflict is always the main plot

questions.question: A character defeats a rival but still feels uncertain about a choice. What can readers infer?
choices: resolving an external conflict may leave an internal conflict

questions.question: A protagonist challenges an unfair school policy through a student council. Which conflict is most central?
A character struggles with guilt after falsely accusing someone. What type of conflict is most directly shown?
A bridge collapse forces two rivals to cooperate against a rising river. How does the setting affect conflict?
choices: it turns the narrator into an antagonist
an environmental threat changes how characters respond to each other

questions.question: A story begins with tension between a person and a rule, then shifts toward the person’s doubts. What changed?
choices: the emphasis moves from external to internal conflict
the point of view becomes second person
the plot loses its central problem

questions.question: An antagonist is not always a person. Which example best demonstrates this?
choices: a character debates whether to apologize
a character tries to survive a blizzard
a student challenges a dress code

questions.question: A student calls every disagreement “character versus society.” Which example best supports a more precise label of character versus character?
choices: two neighbors argue over a shared garden

questions.question: A character cannot control a drought but can choose whether to share water. What interaction is present?
choices: conflict with nature shapes a moral choice
a subplot removes the main goal

questions.question: A story’s main problem ends when the protagonist forgives a rival. Which conclusion is most supported?
choices: the setting has become the antagonist
the story has no internal change
the resolution addresses the relationship conflict
